The test image shows soybean stems with prominent reddish-brown to dark chocolate-brown discoloration/lesions extending along the stems at nodal areas, with dead plant material (dried leaves still attached above). This pattern strongly suggests a stem disease.

Key features:
- Elongated reddish-brown stem lesions/cankers at node regions
- Dead, dried leaves remaining attached to the stems
- Lesions appear to extend over multiple internodes
- No obvious white mold or black fruiting bodies visible

Top candidates: Phytophthora (chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending upward) or Anthracnose (red-brown stem lesions). Let me check the reference.

The Phytophthora reference shows matching features: dark brown stem discoloration at nodes with dead leaves remaining attached, and the characteristic brown stem lesions extending upward. The bottom-right panel shows a close-up node lesion very similar to the test image.

The test image matches Phytophthora well:
- Dark reddish-brown stem discoloration extending over multiple nodes (characteristic diagnostic symptom)
- Dead leaves remaining attached to the stem
- Lesions visible at nodal regions extending upward
